hook: This section of the FBI's 62-HQ-83894 case file opens with Washington Post newspaper clippings from July 7, 1947 covering the initial nationwide flying saucer wave, paired with a classified CIC Sixth Army memorandum documenting first-person law enforcement and military witness accounts of disc sightings over Portland, Oregon on July 4, 1947.
why_it_matters: This file captures the FBI's real-time response to the 1947 flying saucer wave within days of the Kenneth Arnold sighting, documenting both media coverage and credible law enforcement witnesses simultaneously. The CIC agent explicitly vouches for witness reliability, elevating Portland police and Air Corps veteran testimony above civilian reports. The Army's admission that radar nationwide failed to detect the objects — combined with credible multi-witness accounts — establishes the anomalous pattern that drove the formation of formal Air Force investigation programs.

key_findings.finding: A priest near Gratton, Wisconsin recovered a physical sheet metal disc with internal components and reported it to the FBI, representing one of the earliest documented physical evidence cases in the 1947 wave.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: These July 1947 sightings are the founding incidents that prompted the Army Air Forces to launch Project Sign (direct predecessor of Blue Book), making this FBI case file part of the foundational evidence base for the entire Air Force UAP investigation program.

Wright Field is listed among the document entities and Army Air Forces public relations officers are quoted making official statements about ongoing investigations, connecting to the Air Materiel Command at Wright-Patterson that handled physical evidence and technical analysis.

Congress is listed among the document entities and the VFW national commander is quoted claiming he was expecting 'momentarily' information from Washington to explain the discs, reflecting early congressional-level awareness and public pressure.
